raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Motivation GLM-5.3-Flash MTP 5/1/6 decode spends about 5% of each step with the GPU outside CUDA graphs. The largest gap is between the draft-extend and draft graphs, where `DeepseekSparseAttnMultiStepBackend` fills each of the 4 draft-step backends separately, though every step ends up holding identical metadata. ## Modifications - Draft steps 1.. now alias step 0's captured metadata. Replay refreshes step 0 once from the precomputed input, and steps 1.. no longer allocate their own wide `page_table` and seqlen buffers. - `DeepseekSparseAttnBackend` gets two protected helpers: `_init_cuda_graph_state_shared` sizes only the multi-CTA KV counter, which `_forward_trtllm` reads per backend, and `_share_cuda_graph_metadata` aliases step 0's metadata. - Sharing does not depend on KPool fusion, so it replaces both the KPool sibling copies and the multi-destination copy block. - `test_dsa_metadata_replay.py` captures and replays the steps through the wrapper for `index_kpool` 4 (KPool fusion on and off) and 1, and checks that steps share step 0's buffers, only step 0 refreshes, and the result matches the ordinary path. Sharing is safe because every step consumes the same precomputed input and the draft forward only reads the metadata. All writes to `DSAMetadata` / `KPoolWritePlan` are in the init and replay paths; the one forward-time writer (`dsa_npu_indexer.py`) is prefill-only. Only GLM-5.3-Flash sets `index_kpool` (4); DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5 through 5.3 use 1. With more than 3 draft steps, those models used the multi-destination copy block, which never refreshed `paged_mqa_schedule_metadata` / `topk_v2_plan` for the first three steps; they now get the full refresh. Some cleanups this change enables can be done as a follow-up. ## Accuracy Tests sgl-eval 0.1.2 GSM8K, 200 examples, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, thinking on. | Model | GSM8K before | GSM8K after | Accept length (conc. 1) before | Accept length after | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | GLM-5.3-Flash | 99.0% | 98.0% | 4.49 | 4.49 | | GLM-5.3 | 98.5% | 99.5% | 4.19 | 4.19 | `test_dsa_metadata_replay.py`: 3 passed (6 subtests) on GB300. ## Speed Tests and Profiling GLM-5.3-Flash, 4× GB300, `--tp-size 4`, trtllm DSA, fp8_e4m3 KV, `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE, EAGLE 5/1/6, greedy, 2,048 output tokens. Accept length pinned with `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=5 SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token` (5.00 on every run). | | Before | After | |---|---:|---:| | `fwd_occupancy`, concurrency 1 / 8 / 32 | 93.19 / 94.62 / 93.13% | 94.46 / 95.63 / 94.64% | | Per-request decode, concurrency 1 / 8 / 32 | 630 / 372 / 235 tok/s | 639 / 376 / 239 tok/s | | Draft decode graph memory per GPU | 1.02 GB | 0.36 GB | nsys, batch size 1, medians over ~165–185 steps: | | Before | After | |---|---:|---:| | Gap: draft-extend → draft | 286 µs | 175 µs | | Gap: draft → verify | 684 µs | 363 µs | | GPU idle per step | 884 µs | 619 µs | | `fused_metadata_copy_kernel` per step | 4 | 0 | | Eager memcpys per step | 51 | 24 | The draft → verify gap also shrinks because the verify graph launch waits on host work: with less of it during draft replay, the launch lands sooner. The draft-extend → draft gap of the median step (by that gap), same 400 µs scale, starting 40 µs before the draft-extend graph ends: **Before:** the copy ladder, including 4 `fused_metadata_copy_kernel`, runs until the draft graph starts at ~326 µs. **After:** only step 0's refresh remains; the draft graph starts at ~215 µs. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #38664087872](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38664087872) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #38664087888](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38664087888) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #38664087886](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38664087886)
